Let me start by saying this, I am a native Cincinnatian. I like Cincinnati style chili. I have eaten at this location for many years and have had very little issues (to be honest I can't remember any issues if I ever had any). That being said they have expanded their menu. And because of this, I must give my opinions.

Goldstar then (realizing this) decided to take their fry game to the next level. Their fully loaded bacon chili cheese fries are heavenly. I highly recommend them.

B. Their classic chicken sandwhich is pretty decent. I was surprised how good it was. But if you are in the mood for a chicken sandwich, you should go to Chick'fil-a instead. They aren't special, just pretty good. They put pickles and a special sauce on it. The special sauce makes it worth it.

C. Their Hamburgers and Sandwhiches are so-so. Their special sauce is good but price vs performance, they aren't special. You aren't missing anything with the burgers or sandwhiches.

D. Skyline is better than Goldstar but not by much and only on 3-Ways and Coneys. I believe Goldstar has a smaller coney. But to be honest, Skyline and Goldstar are comparable and you can't go wrong with either. Around here in Cincinnati, this opinion might get you in trouble. But I assure you, they are both good.

E. I miss firehouse style. That was amazing. Please bring it back.

I took my wife and 11 1/2 month old son here on a whim, on a Saturday evening, as a surprise, having never been before, and decided based on Google reviews. We went at 615pm when Google said it was peak time and expected a wait of about 15-30 minutes based on Google. About half of the tables were empty and no one was at the small bar they have. Look, we took an almost one month old baby to a restaurant we'd never been to before and having never done this by ourselves since this is our first child and first time eating out without friends or family. I was half prepared to be asked to leave, get into an argument with other patrons over his random screeching when he wanted another veggie stick, or leave feeling guilty for having left a trail of a disaster behind.

Before we could even think about one of us taking the baby to the car while the other paid, we had the desert, the food boxed up, the check, paid, tipped, and were walking out.

If you’re a sushi purist, this place may not be the best choice for you. However if you’re like me and enjoy Americanized sushi, you have to give this place a try. It’s the “Chipotle of sushi” in a way, and I love everything about it. They have pre-designed selections you can pick if you want, or you can go down the line picking which protein(s), veggies, sauces, and toppings you want on your bowl or roll. This means you can go as simple or as crazy as you want, and as traditional or unconventional as you’d like.

The prices end up being a bit higher than your average counter-serve restaurant, but it’s absolutely worth it for the quality of the food and the portion size. I also highly recommend shelling out the $2.50 for a fountain drink. It killed me a little at first, but their fresh and unique drinks are amazing. Combine that with the friendly service, dedication to the environment (almost everything they use is compostable) and wide variety of ingredients to add to your meal, I don’t know how anyone could not like this place. Definitely give Fusian a try if you haven’t yet!

Just to give you an idea, here are *some* of the options they have (don’t yell at me if/when they change):
- Bowl with white or brown rice, with or without kale; roll with white or brown rice and soy paper or seaweed
- Proteins: Raw tuna, raw salmon, smoked salmon, shrimp tempura, chicken, tofu
- Veggies: carrots, beets, asparagus, jalapeños, pineapple (awesome on a bowl!)
- Toppings: sesame seeds, almonds, tempura crunch, scallions, and as always ginger and wasabi available on the side
- Drinks: agave, strawberry, or lavender lemonade, agave gingerade, subtly sweet black tea, unsweet green tea

Last but not least, a restaurant in the Short North that is quite easily kid friendly? Awesome. They even have kid sized offerings.

text:
Had two-starred this place for a while since the lobby was still closed--in July--due to COVID and Taco Bell franchise owner was not willing to put up dividers for the staff. This kept a lot of money from flowing through here from first responders, semi truck drivers, bicyclists and people without cars since the locals know that the drive-thru here is incredibly narrow with a short clearance. Fortunately, they've changed course and the lobby and dine-in are now open, socially distanced.

There are a few changes at this location to minimize contact to COVID. For one the sauce packets, tissues and forks are all behind the counter and you must ask for them or specify how many you want when placing a mobile order. For soda cups, refills are still possible, but you must ask for new cup. Neither are bad things given the circumstances so I'm not dinging for that.

It's four stars because prices are a bit high for the area, and sometimes you taste a batch of bad lettuce or onions. However, apart from that, it's all around a good experience with friendly staff.

This leads to longer-than-average wait times for food that seems to be a bit on the pricey side. Burgers, sandwiches and entrees here are tasty, but do not offer anything that you can't find done better elsewhere. The sandwich I enjoyed my first visit was good, and the burger I had the following time was passable, but not the experiences you expect to receive when your meal is $20 by the time the check comes.

text:
JUST STAY AWAY!  Here's why ...

I believe Unique Coney Island (UCI) used to be National Coney Island (NCI).  I think someone who worked at NCI or owned this NCI franchise (Sterling Heights), sold it and opened UCI immediately after.  The food at NCI was oftentimes so bad, I actually got sick on a couple of occasions (food poisoning).  I tried to report them to the local health department, but their reporting process was so drawn out, I just dropped it.  Carryout breakfast often appeared as if food had been transferred from someone's plate (who didn't eat it) into a carryout container, then resold at full price. Because UCI is in my area, I said to myself ... "Okay!  I'll try this place.  Maybe it's totally new ownership!!".  WRONG!!  Same bad food, and I think same chef ...

When I walked into UCI tonight, the chef looked like the same chef that worked at NCI.  Really hungry, I decided to play it safe an only order a chicken greek and 2 spinach pies, to be split between a friend and myself.  The spinach pies were DISGUSTING!!  These weren't typical spinach pies.  These appeared as if the chef sprayed them with Pam, threw them on the grill, then flattened them!!  Who eats re-grilled, flattened spinach pies?  Even the lingering taste left in your mouth was really odd.  (See pic showing grease on white paper towel after dabbing just a single side of one spinach pie).

Now, onto the Greek Chicken salad ...

The salad was much better, but even this was bad.  After looking at the spinach pies, my friend refused to eat the salad.  (I think I should have followed her lead.)  The chicken was cut into strips like french fries.  It was as if the chicken was cooked yesterday, left out all day, then thrown in the fridge overnight, then brought back out the following day and recooked on the grill.  The feta cheese was odd.  There were portions where the cheese was chunky and chewy, and the Greek dressing was tasteless.

It's sad when you're hungry and you "PAY" a restaurant to feed you, yet you can't eat the food.  But, ironically, 30 minutes after eating the spinach pie and a little of the salad, I ended up with -- diarrhea.  AGAIN!

This is likely why I don't see many cars in the parking lot of this restaurant.  Folks, stay away from this restaurant!!  They don't value you as a customer and could care less about serving you bad food.

Reporting these places to the health department is a little complicated.  But it's nice knowing reviews exists to warn others.

If I could give this review a title it would be "Worst Valentine's Day Ever at Milwaukee's "Most Romantic Restaurant!" My boyfriend and I went to the pasta tree for Valentine's Day yesterday. Our bad experience started when I called to make a reservation and no one would answer the phone! I called three times on two different days trying to speak to someone on staff. I finally gave in and made the reservation online as their voicemail suggested. We were both looking forward to a wonderful, romantic meal when we began the hour drive to the restaurant. On the way I was concerned we would be late for our reservation due to traffic (we weren't) so I called three times to let the staff know and once again, no one answered the phone. When we arrived the host seemed preoccupied and did not greet us, just immediately asked if we had a reservation. I told him we did and that I had received a gift certificate from LivingSocial for Christmas. He very rudely and brusquely gestured to the paper and said "oh, we don't take those on Valentine's. It says it somewhere on there." We thought this was a little odd since we had read the fine print pretty carefully before making the reservation but were willing to use it another time. The host walked away from us with no other words that I heard. After a few seconds we realized we were to follow him but he was already pretty far ahead of us. He walked into an area that appeared to be a kitchen so we stopped, unsure if we were to follow (kind of gross to have cusomers walk basically through the kitchen in my opinion). After a few seconds he came back and waved us in to follow him into a second dining area beyond our view. He brought us to a table and left us and said our server would be (Sara?). While we waited for the server, I started to read the gift certificate again to see the exclusions. While we were reading our server came by and rudely and abruptly told me we couldn't use the certificate. She then asked us our drink order and handed the two of us ONE menu. At this point we both felt extremely  uncomfortable and unwelcome. While she was gone I continued to read the certificate to find that Valentine's was not listed as an exclusion! When the server returned she asked how we were doing. I replied "honestly, not great. We received this certificate as a gift and are unable to use it after driving an hour to get here, even though Valentine's Day is not listed in the exclusions!" The server's tone was immediately combative and all she had to say was that they have never accepted the certificates on Valentines, that is said it wasn't valid  on the website it was purchased on, and that they couldn't do anything to help us. To this I replied that "this had been an extremely negative experience" and that I thought "we were just going to leave." All the server had to say in response was "ok." No apology, no sympathy, no kindness of any sort. To add insult to injury, on our way out the host walked past and said "have a nice night", in a tone that almost seemed to imply he had expected it to happen when we walked in 20 minutes prior.

Now I understand that a business might have policies in place about when a certificate can or cannot be used, but the bottom line is that it was not listed under the exclusions on the gift we received. Whether the website was updated after the purchase of the gift is irrelevant. They should have at least offered an apology for the inconvenience. Not to mention that they made us feel unwelcome and like our patronage was not wanted from the second we got there until the second we left. Between the two of us, we have almost 20 years of retail and food service experience and both are department managers at a successful, local business, so we know bad service when we see it. We agree that this was the worst customer service either of us have EVER experienced. Needless to say, we are apalled and extremely dissapointed with the staff's actions. So, if you are picking your next date night restaurant, I would advise you keep looking.

Nope, nope, nope... I was expecting so much more. We were bummed they don't accept reservations. I had called yesterday to be on the phone list, which supposedly cuts down on your wait time. We ended up waiting over a half hour. We put our order in quickly and had requested some bread and olive oil. text:
More Miss Than Hit. Decided to go to the BelAir Cantina  on Sunday after some shopping. The reviews looked good and it was close by. My daughter and I were seated by a server and told the brunch was available or we could order off the menu. When the server for our table came to get our drink order she took the menus and said we had been given the wrong ones. Ok, no big deal. We got the new menus and discovered that the items we had wanted were not offered during brunch. She dropped off chips and three dipping sauces/salsas - salsa Verde,  Roasted salsa & spicy Arbol. Only the salsa Verde had flavor. The roasted salsa  was made up of charred bits of tomato skin and tasted more burnt than roasted. The spicy Arbol looked like pale tomato soup and tasted  like it. Please do not label something as "spicy" if it has no flavor. Disappointing.
We each ordered three tacos (of varying ingredients) with rice, black beans & pinto beans. The food came out very quickly and, besides the skin on top of the beans, looked very appetizing. Sadly, the food was not. I don't know how all the flavor can be sucked out of food but these folks have discovered the secret. The meats were dry & tasteless. The carnitas was chewy & and the only flavor was from the pico. The carne asada was dry and tasteless. The pollo verde suffered a similar fate as the carnitas - chewy, stringy bits of bland meat that we're overpowered by the condiments they came with.
The slaw that came with the shrimp tasted raw and did not seem to be dressed with any citrus. Finally, the gringo was an unseasoned pile of ground beef. The rice,  even though it looked as though it had been cooked with, carrots, corn, peas and seasoning managed to taste exactly like white rice and nothing else. The best part (part that had flavor) of the meal were the beans. The black beans were pureed baby food but had a nice flavor while the pinto beans had flavor and chunks of beans.
Painted on some tables and tagged on the menu is the tagline "I'LL go if you go" and I understand now that this is either a dare or the most lackluster endorsement for a restaurant. I would not recommend this place unless you have been placed on a bland diet by your doctor.

text:
I needed to update my review (9/2018) for this restaurant. Since they opened almost a year ago, the food has changed as the menu did too. I changed from 5 stars to 2 as the food isn’t as good as it was when they first opened. Portions are smaller and they didn’t have the thum-garlic sauce when we went in this time. Sadly, I wouldn’t go in here again. They had a great concept and should have stuck with it.
———————————————-
We went there yesterday (almost a year ago) and we Loved it! The concept of having 5 meats to choose from and a vast array of toppings was excellent. They also offered 2 types of halal meat! They have 2 types of rice to choose either saffron (you could really taste it in the rice too) and brown rice with lime and cilantro (nice tang) . They give you a generous portion of meat and have a vast array of sauces to select . I had the Thom sauce (garlicy mayonnaise type) it was delicious on my American gyro meat plate! My daughter had the donner (Turkish style meat) that was delicious too. The falafels were homemade too and tasted really good. To top all that off, we tried the baklava. That is the best baklava I have had in years! You could taste real butter in the phyllo dough and real honey not sugar syrup like the other places use! Hands down winner for a great fun place to go with anyone! They have something for everyone there. Spicy, herby, hot, earthy tastes etc.... The owner was very nice and really cared and took an interest if you were enjoying your food. We needed this local place badly as all the other places skimp on ingredients and meat portions and charge too much. This place is perfect price and ample portions on your plate! They weren’t afraid of giving you exactly how much you wanted! Definitely my new go to place as there are so many combinations of meat and fresh ingredients to try!
